done_when: An empty commit whose message has a Functional check paragraph counts as the branch's functional check, and a changed functional check makes close and forge-pr-check treat the earlier review as stale and review again; Forge's own record commits still never count

findings.body: A commit changing only `plans/manual walkthrough.md` is incorrectly treated as worker code: `.split()` produces `plans/manual` and `walkthrough.md`, so the bookkeeping-prefix check fails. If that commit follows a valid functional check, its message replaces the check with an empty string, unnecessarily invalidating the review and potentially restoring the missing-check blocker. `BOOKKEEPING` explicitly excludes all of `plans/` (src/forge/review.py:30). Use NUL-delimited output and split on NUL, filtering empty entries; this also handles Git's quoted filenames correctly. See the [git-diff-tree documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-diff-tree#Documentation/git-diff-tree.txt--z).
findings.title: Preserve filename boundaries when identifying bookkeeping commits

why: A worker's hand walkthrough recorded in an empty commit is ignored: the functional check skips commits that change no files, and close reuses the earlier review because the code didn't move, so the same 'functional check missing' finding blocks forever
